problem.p: An update of a kajenn application replaces its process. Everything the process keeps in memory is lost at that moment: the sessions, so every user signs in again, and the state shared by the pages, for example the chat of a meeting room.

The application this came from is Meetlot (kajenn-webrtc): one Kubernetes Deployment with one replica and strategy: Recreate. Each deploy signs everybody out and closes the PageStore WebSocket of every open page.
The same application needs session lifetimes that depend on where the user signed in: a desktop app should keep its user signed in for months, a browser on a shared computer for a couple of hours.

section.title: kajenn today
section.fact: RequestRegistry registers every operation on entry and drops it on exit: an http dispatch, a WSX message, a kbus frame, a task. It counts operations, not connections.
await_drain(timeout) waits for the in-flight set to empty and returns how many operations are still open when the timeout runs out.
While the server state is not RUNNING, a new http call gets 503 Server restarting with Retry-After: 5.
Shutdown turns the state, drains the registry for at most SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (10 s), then runs the on_shutdown hooks and closes the databases.
WebSocketRegistry keeps the live sockets and the socket each page speaks on, and already accepts a page that reconnects on a new socket before the old one closes.
A session expires after ttl seconds without requests: every request refreshes last_access.
MemorySessionStore.save_snapshot and load_snapshot write and read one pickle of the session objects through pathlib.Path, outside the storage nodes.
Only kajenn serve <name> arms the snapshot; a server built directly with AsgiServer has none.

section.title: 1. One process per application

rule.why: A kajenn process keeps state in memory; Kubernetes replicas would split it.

section.rule: A kajenn application runs as one Kubernetes replica. Several processes are kajenn-orchestra's job.

section.title: 2. Every file goes through a storage node

rule.why: The deployment chooses where the data lives — pod disk, persistent volume, S3 — and the write can be encrypted.

section.rule: Every read and write of a file goes through a genro-storage node of the server's StorageManager. A direct pathlib access is a bug.

section.title: 3. The update is a handover

list.item: The new process starts and gets ready, without traffic.
The old process turns its state: a new call gets 503 with Retry-After.
The old process drains its registry, with a time limit. At the limit the operations still open end with an explicit error.
The old process writes the snapshot of its durable state.
The new process loads the snapshot.
The route of Traefik moves from the old process to the new one.
The old process closes its WebSockets with code 1012 Service Restart and stops.

section.p: The old process stays alive with its state until the new one is ready and verified. If the new one fails, the route does not move and the old process returns to RUNNING.
kajenn-orchestra drives the handover: it knows both processes and the storage.

diagram.title: Handover between the old and the new process

section.diagram: sequenceDiagram participant O as Orchestra participant Old as Old process participant New as New process participant St as Storage node participant T as Traefik O->>New: start, no traffic New-->>O: ready O->>Old: leave Old->>Old: state not RUNNING, new calls get 503 Old->>Old: drain registry (bounded) Old->>St: write snapshot (TYTX, encrypted) O->>New: load snapshot New->>St: read snapshot New-->>O: loaded and verified O->>T: route to New Old->>Old: close WebSockets with 1012, stop

section.title: 4. Calls during the handover
section.p: A call that arrives while the old process is leaving is refused with 503 and Retry-After, as kajenn does today. The old process keeps no call waiting and never proxies.
section.rule: The Gramlot client transport repeats a call refused with 503 after Retry-After. One place, valid for every page.

section.title: 5. WebSockets are rebuilt, not moved
section.p: An open connection cannot move between processes. At the switch the old process closes it with 1012; the client reconnects with the same pageId; the new process rebuilds the page state from the durable state.

rule.why: It keeps the snapshot small and independent of the pages' code.

section.rule: Put the volatile state of a single page in the snapshot.

section.title: 6. The snapshot

list.item: Content: the durable state only — the sessions and the state shared by the pages of an application (for example the state of a meeting room).
Format: plain data, lists and dicts, serialized as TYTX. TYTX keeps dates, decimals and bytes that plain JSON loses.
Place: a storage node, written encrypted. The write is atomic: a temporary node, then a rename.

rule.why: Pickled objects break when a class changes between the old and the new release, and loading a tampered pickle runs code.

section.rule: Write pickled objects in a snapshot.

rule.why: The old and the new process run different releases.

section.rule: A reader of the snapshot tolerates missing keys (default value) and ignores the keys it does not know.
section.p: The snapshot is armed by the configuration of the site, not by the command that starts the server.

table.title: Lifetime without requests, renewed by every request

list.item: The login method sets the lifetime of its session when it attaches the identity, through a public API of the session.
The cookie lasts longer than any session: the server is the only judge of expiry.
An administrator can close the sessions of a user.
The groups of the identity provider are read again periodically, not only at sign-in: a user removed from an administrators' group loses the rights within that period, not at the end of the session.

decision.question: What happens to a call that arrives during the handover?

option.title: Refused with 503 and Retry-After, repeated by the client
Held by the old process and forwarded to the new one

decision.choice: No call stays hanging in the old process; kajenn already answers so.

decision.question: Which format does the snapshot use?

option.title: Plain data in TYTX, encrypted on a storage node

decision.choice: No class versions between releases, types kept, no code run when reading.

decision.question: Who runs several processes of one application?
decision.choice: Kubernetes replicas would split the state a kajenn process keeps in memory.

decision.question: How long does the old process wait for the open operations, and what does it answer them at the limit?
How often are the groups of the identity provider read again for a long session?

list.item: An update signs nobody out and leaves no gap in the answers; open pages reconnect.
A crash still loses what changed after the last snapshot: accepted.
The deployment chooses where the snapshot lives without touching the application.
The Gramlot client gains two behaviours used by every page: repeat on 503, reconnect on 1012.
